questions: What is the golden rule for a personal account?
Debit the receiver; credit the giver
Debit what goes out; credit what comes in
Debit the giver; credit the receiver
Personal accounts follow the receiver/giver rule: debit the receiver and credit the giver.
What is the golden rule for a real account?
Debit what comes in; credit what goes out
Debit the giver; credit the receiver
Debit all income; credit all losses
Real accounts represent assets. An asset coming in is debited; an asset going out is credited.
Which rule applies to nominal accounts?
Debit expenses and losses; credit incomes and gains
Debit incomes and gains; credit expenses and losses
Debit the receiver; credit the giver
Nominal accounts record expenses, losses, incomes, and gains.
In the traditional classification, Cash A/c is which type?
Cash is a tangible asset, so Cash A/c is a real account.
In the traditional classification, Furniture A/c is which type?
Furniture is an asset owned by the business, so its account is real.
In the traditional classification, Machinery A/c is which type?
Machinery is a tangible asset. Buying it creates an asset rather than an immediate machinery expense.
Rent Expense A/c belongs to which traditional class?
Rent consumed by the business is an expense, so it is nominal.
Salary Expense A/c belongs to which traditional class?
Salary expense measures a cost of operating the business, so it is nominal.
Commission Income A/c is which type of account?
Commission earned is income. Nominal accounts record incomes and gains as well as expenses and losses.
Interest Expense A/c is which traditional account type?
Interest expense is a business cost and is therefore a nominal account.
Depreciation Expense A/c is classified as what?
Depreciation expense records the allocation of an asset's cost over its useful life. The expense account is nominal.
Bad Debts Expense A/c is classified as what?
Bad debts expense records a loss from an uncollectible receivable, so it is nominal.
Riya A/c, a customer's account, is which traditional type?
Riya is an individual person. Her account is a natural personal account.
ABC Ltd A/c is which kind of personal account?
A company is a legal or artificial person, so its account is an artificial personal account.
Under traditional classification, a bank's account is generally what?
A bank is an institution, so its account is traditionally artificial personal. Under modern classification, a positive bank balance is an asset.
A registered charity's account is which traditional type?
An organisation is treated as an artificial person in the traditional account classification.
In traditional classification, outstanding salaries can be represented by which account type?
Outstanding Salaries A/c represents amounts owed to employees, so it is a representative personal account.
You pay a supplier against an existing payable. On which side is the supplier's personal account recorded?
Both sides for the full amount
The supplier receives payment, so debit the receiver. This also reduces the payable.
You buy goods on credit from Meera. Which side is Meera A/c recorded on?
Meera supplies value to the business. Credit the giver, creating a payable to her.
A customer pays an existing invoice in cash. Which side is the customer's personal account recorded on?
No entry because the sale was already recorded
The customer gives cash to the business. Credit the customer and debit Cash, reducing the receivable.
A laptop is bought for business use with cash. Which side is Laptop A/c recorded on?
The laptop comes into the business. For its real account, debit what comes in.
Cash is paid for office rent. Which side is Cash A/c recorded on?
Cash leaves the business, so credit Cash A/c under the real-account rule.
Office electricity expense is incurred. Which side is Electricity Expense A/c recorded on?
Electricity used by the office is an expense. Debit expenses and losses.
Consulting income is earned. Which side is Consulting Income A/c recorded on?
Consulting income is revenue, so credit incomes and gains.
Insurance expense for the current period belongs on which side?
Insurance consumed during the period is an expense, so its nominal account is debited.
A customer debt is written off as bad debt. Which side is Bad Debts Expense A/c recorded on?
An uncollectible debt is a loss. Debit Bad Debts Expense and credit the customer's receivable.
A gain on disposal of equipment is recognised. Which side is the gain account recorded on?
A gain is credited under the nominal-account rule. The asset disposal entry is recorded separately as part of the full transaction.
Which pair both contains real accounts?
Cash and furniture are assets. The other pairs contain nominal accounts or personal accounts.
Which pair both contains nominal accounts?
Nominal accounts include both expenses and incomes, so rent expense and commission income are both nominal.
What should you identify before applying a golden rule?
The account type and its role in the transaction
Classify each affected account and understand what it receives, gives, earns, or incurs before choosing debit and credit.
Under the modern approach, an increase in an asset is recorded as what?
Assets normally have debit balances. Debit an increase and credit a decrease.
Under the modern approach, a decrease in an asset is recorded as what?
An asset decreases through a credit, such as crediting Cash when money is paid out.
An increase in a liability is recorded on which side?
Both sides of that same liability
Liabilities normally carry credit balances. An increase is credited.
A decrease in a liability is recorded on which side?
Debit a liability to reduce it, such as debiting a supplier when paying a bill.
An increase in the owner's capital is normally recorded as what?
Capital is equity and normally has a credit balance. Additional capital is credited.
A direct reduction in an equity account is normally recorded as what?
Equity normally has a credit balance, so a debit reduces it.
An increase in revenue is recorded on which side?
Revenue increases equity through profit and normally carries a credit balance.
An increase in a business expense is recorded on which side?
Expenses normally have debit balances. An expense increase is debited.
Which balance is normal for Drawings A/c?
Drawings reduce owner's equity and normally have a debit balance.
Which balance is normal for Accounts Receivable?
Receivables are assets representing money due from customers. Their normal balance is debit.
Which balance is normal for Accounts Payable?
Payables are liabilities representing amounts owed to suppliers. Their normal balance is credit.
Which balance is normal for Sales Revenue A/c?
Sales revenue is income, so its normal balance is credit.
Cash is introduced by the owner. What happens to Cash A/c?
Cash is an asset entering the business, so its increase is debited.
The owner introduces cash as capital. What happens to Capital A/c?
It is treated as a loss
The owner's investment increases equity. Credit Capital A/c.
A loan is received in the bank. What happens to Loan Payable A/c?
It is counted as sales income
The business now owes the lender more, so credit the increased liability.
Loan principal is repaid. What happens to Loan Payable A/c?
It is debited as interest expense
Repaying principal reduces the loan liability, so debit Loan Payable. Interest, if any, is a separate expense.
Office salaries for the current month are paid. What happens to Salary Expense A/c?
Salaries for the current period are an expense. Debit Salary Expense.
A service is provided on credit. What happens to the customer's receivable?
It is treated as cash paid
It is omitted until cash is received
The customer now owes the business, increasing an asset. Debit Accounts Receivable.
A customer settles an existing receivable by bank transfer. What happens to the customer's account?
Collection reduces the customer's receivable, so credit the customer's account.
A supplier is paid against an existing bill. What happens to the supplier's payable?
It is recorded as a new purchase again
Payment reduces what is owed to the supplier. Debit the supplier's account.
Furniture is purchased for office use on credit. What happens to Furniture A/c?
It is always charged to rent
Furniture is a business asset. Its acquisition increases the asset, so debit Furniture.
Business cash is withdrawn by the owner for personal use. What happens to Drawings A/c?
It is treated as salary expense
A personal withdrawal is drawings, not a business expense. Debit Drawings and credit Cash.
Interest is earned and received in the bank. What happens to Interest Income A/c?
Interest earned is income. Credit Interest Income while debiting Bank.
Bank charges are deducted from a positive bank balance. What happens to Bank Charges Expense A/c?
Bank charges are a business expense. Debit Bank Charges and credit Bank.
Annual insurance is paid in advance and initially recorded as an asset. What happens to Prepaid Insurance A/c?
Prepaid insurance represents a future benefit. The asset increases through a debit.
Part of prepaid insurance expires. What happens to Prepaid Insurance A/c?
The future benefit decreases as insurance is consumed. Credit Prepaid Insurance and debit Insurance Expense.
Rent has been incurred but remains unpaid. What happens to Rent Payable A/c?
Unpaid rent creates a liability. Credit Rent Payable and debit Rent Expense.
Previously accrued rent is paid. What happens to Rent Payable A/c?
It creates rent expense a second time
Paying the accrued amount reduces the liability. Debit Rent Payable; do not recognise the same expense twice.
Depreciation is recorded using an accumulated-depreciation account. Which side is Accumulated Depreciation recorded on?
Accumulated Depreciation is a contra-asset account with a normal credit balance. Debit Depreciation Expense and credit it.
A customer's uncollectible balance is written off. What happens to the customer's receivable?
Writing off the balance reduces receivables. Credit the customer's account and debit Bad Debts Expense in a direct write-off example.
Using the periodic inventory approach, goods are bought for resale. What happens to Purchases A/c?
Under the periodic approach, purchases of goods for resale are debited to Purchases A/c.
Using a separate purchase-returns account, goods are returned to a supplier. What happens to Purchase Returns A/c?
Purchase returns reduce purchases. The separate Purchase Returns account normally has a credit balance.
A customer returns goods and Sales Returns A/c is used. Which side is Sales Returns recorded on?
Sales Returns is a contra-revenue account. Debit it to reduce net sales.
Settlement discount is allowed to a customer and treated as an expense. Which side is Discount Allowed A/c recorded on?
Discount Allowed reduces the amount recovered and is debited in this expense treatment.
Settlement discount is received from a supplier and treated as income. Which side is Discount Received A/c recorded on?
Under this income treatment, Discount Received is a gain and is credited.
Which balance is normal for Accumulated Depreciation?
This contra-asset account offsets asset cost and normally carries a credit balance.
A refundable security deposit is paid to a landlord. Which side is Security Deposit A/c recorded on?
The refundable deposit is an asset recoverable from the landlord. Debit Security Deposit and credit Cash or Bank.
A customer pays in advance for work not yet performed. Which side is Unearned Revenue A/c recorded on?
The advance creates an obligation to provide the service. Credit Unearned Revenue, a liability.
Work covered by a customer advance is now completed. Which side is Unearned Revenue A/c recorded on?
Earning the advance reduces the liability. Debit Unearned Revenue and credit Service Revenue.
Do debit and credit always mean increase and decrease respectively?
No; the effect depends on the account type
Only when a bank is involved
Debit means left and credit means right. A debit increases assets and expenses but decreases liabilities and equity.
The owner starts a business with ₹50,000 cash. Which entry is correct?
Cash increases by ₹50,000 and owner's equity increases by the same amount. Debit Cash and credit Capital.
The owner deposits ₹80,000 of personal funds into the business bank account. Which entry is correct?
The business bank asset and owner's capital both increase. This is capital introduced, not sales.
Office rent of ₹8,000 is paid in cash for the current month. Which entry is correct?
Rent is an expense and cash leaves the business. Debit Rent Expense and credit Cash.
Office salaries of ₹20,000 are paid by bank transfer for the current month. Which entry is correct?
Recognise salary expense with a debit and reduce Bank with a credit.
Goods worth ₹12,000 are sold for cash. Ignore GST and inventory-cost entries. Which entry records the sale?
Cash received increases the asset and the sale increases revenue. Debit Cash and credit Sales.
Goods worth ₹15,000 are sold to Riya on credit. Ignore GST and inventory-cost entries. Which entry records the sale?
Riya owes the business, so debit her receivable. Credit Sales to record income.
Goods worth ₹9,000 are bought for resale in cash under the periodic approach. Ignore GST. Which entry is correct?
Record goods for resale in Purchases under the periodic approach and credit the cash paid.
Goods worth ₹18,000 are bought on credit from Karan under the periodic approach. Ignore GST. Which entry is correct?
Debit Purchases for goods bought and credit Karan because the business owes him.
₹6,000 is paid to Karan against an existing supplier bill. Which entry is correct?
Paying an existing bill reduces Karan's payable. Debit Karan and credit Cash; do not record the purchase again.
Riya pays ₹7,000 by bank transfer against an existing invoice. Which entry is correct?
Collection increases Bank and reduces Riya's receivable. The sale was already recognised.
Office furniture costing ₹25,000 is purchased in cash. Which entry is correct?
Furniture used by the business is a fixed asset, not trading goods. Debit Furniture and credit Cash.
A business vehicle costing ₹3,00,000 is bought on credit from Auto Ltd. Which entry is correct?
Recognise the vehicle asset and the payable to Auto Ltd. Both increase.
The owner withdraws ₹3,000 cash for personal use. Which entry is correct?
Personal withdrawals are drawings, not business expenses. Debit Drawings and credit Cash.
A bank loan of ₹1,00,000 is credited to the business bank account. Which entry is correct?
The bank asset increases and a loan liability is created. Loan proceeds are not revenue.
₹10,000 of loan principal is repaid by bank transfer. No interest is included. Which entry is correct?
Principal repayment reduces the loan liability. Debit Loan Payable and credit Bank.
₹2,000 of loan interest is paid by bank transfer. Which entry is correct?
Interest is an expense separate from loan principal. Debit Interest Expense and credit Bank.
Commission income of ₹4,000 is received in cash. Which entry is correct?
Cash increases and commission earned is income. Debit Cash and credit Commission Income.
The bank deducts ₹500 in bank charges. Which entry is correct?
Bank Charges Expense Dr; Bank Cr
Bank Dr; Bank Charges Expense Cr
Bank Charges Expense Dr; Sales Cr
Bank charges are an expense and the bank balance falls. Debit the expense and credit Bank.
The bank credits ₹1,200 interest earned to the account. Which entry is correct?
Interest earned increases Bank and income. Debit Bank and credit Interest Income.
₹5,000 of electricity expense is incurred but unpaid. Which entry is correct?
Electricity Expense Dr; Electricity Payable Cr
The expense belongs to the current period even before payment. Credit a payable rather than cash or bank.
Previously accrued electricity expense of ₹5,000 is paid from the bank. Which entry is correct?
Electricity Expense Dr; Bank Cr again
Settle the existing liability by debiting Electricity Payable. Do not charge the same expense twice.
₹12,000 is paid for future insurance coverage and recorded initially as an asset. Which entry is correct?
The payment buys a future benefit. Debit Prepaid Insurance and credit Bank.
₹1,000 of prepaid insurance is consumed this month. Which adjusting entry is correct?
Insurance Expense Dr; Prepaid Insurance Cr
Prepaid Insurance Dr; Insurance Expense Cr
Insurance Expense Dr; Bank Cr again
Recognise the consumed portion as expense and reduce the prepaid asset. No new payment occurs.
₹8,000 depreciation is recorded using accumulated depreciation. Which entry is correct?
Depreciation Expense Dr; Accumulated Depreciation Cr
Depreciation is a non-cash expense. Credit Accumulated Depreciation, a contra-asset account.
A customer's ₹2,500 debt is written off using the direct write-off method. Which entry is correct?
Bad Debts Expense Dr; Customer Cr
Customer Dr; Bad Debts Expense Cr
Bad Debts Expense Dr; Sales Cr
Debit the bad-debt loss and credit the customer to remove the uncollectible receivable.
A customer returns ₹3,000 of goods sold on credit. Ignore GST and inventory entries; use Sales Returns. Which entry is correct?
Debit Sales Returns to reduce net sales and credit the customer's receivable.
₹2,000 of goods bought on credit are returned to the supplier. Use Purchase Returns. Which entry is correct?
The return reduces the supplier payable and purchases. Debit the supplier and credit Purchase Returns.
A customer owing ₹10,000 pays ₹9,800 cash in full settlement. Treat ₹200 discount allowed as expense. Which entry is correct?
Cash Dr 9,800 + Discount Allowed Dr 200; Customer Cr 10,000
Cash Dr 10,000; Customer Cr 9,800 + Discount Allowed Cr 200
The entire receivable is cleared: debit cash received and discount allowed, then credit the customer ₹10,000.
A supplier owed ₹10,000 accepts ₹9,700 by bank in full settlement. Treat discount received as income. Which entry is correct?
Supplier Dr 10,000; Bank Cr 9,700 + Discount Received Cr 300
Bank Dr 9,700 + Discount Received Dr 300; Supplier Cr 10,000
Debit the full payable cleared, credit the bank payment, and credit the ₹300 settlement gain.
₹20,000 business cash is deposited into the business bank account. Which entry is correct?
This transfers one business asset to another. Debit Bank and credit Cash; it is neither income nor new capital.
₹5,000 is withdrawn from the business bank account for office cash. Which entry is correct?
The funds remain in the business. Debit Cash and credit Bank; this is not personal drawings.
₹4,000 is paid for office stationery consumed immediately. Which entry is correct?
Consumed stationery is a current expense, so debit Stationery Expense and credit Cash.
₹6,000 is paid for routine equipment repairs. No improvement is created. Which entry is correct?
Routine repairs maintain the asset and are expensed. A qualifying improvement would have different treatment.
A refundable office security deposit of ₹30,000 is paid by bank. Which entry is correct?
A refundable deposit is recoverable and is an asset, not rent expense.
A customer pays ₹15,000 in advance for services not yet provided. Which entry is correct?
Bank Dr; Service Revenue Cr immediately
The business owes future service, so the advance is a liability until earned.
Services worth ₹15,000 covered by a customer advance are now completed. Which entry is correct?
Unearned Revenue Dr; Service Revenue Cr
Bank Dr; Service Revenue Cr again
Service Revenue Dr; Unearned Revenue Cr
Reduce the advance liability and recognise earned revenue. No second cash receipt occurs.
Consulting work worth ₹18,000 is completed on credit. Which entry is correct?
Recognise a receivable and earned consulting revenue even though collection happens later.
Accrued salary of ₹9,000 must be recognised at month-end. Which entry is correct?
Salary Expense Dr; Salary Payable Cr
Salary Payable Dr; Salary Expense Cr
Salary already earned by employees is an expense and creates a payable when unpaid.
₹7,000 of interest is earned but not yet received. Which entry is correct?
Interest Receivable Dr; Interest Income Cr
Interest Expense Dr; Interest Payable Cr
Interest Income Dr; Interest Receivable Cr
Accrued income creates an asset receivable. Record income when earned under accrual accounting.
A ₹5,000 consulting receipt was credited to Capital by mistake. Which entry corrects only the wrong classification?
Bank Dr; Consulting Revenue Cr again
Debit Capital to remove the mistaken credit and credit Consulting Revenue. Bank was correctly debited already.
A ledger's main purpose is to do what?
The journal records events in order; the ledger collects each account's debits and credits.
Moving an entry from the journal to the relevant ledger is called what?
Posting transfers the debit and credit effects to the individual ledger accounts.
Where is the debit side of a traditional T-account?
A T-account shows debits on the left and credits on the right.
Where is the credit side of a traditional T-account?
The credit side is the right side; debit is the left side.
Cash starts at zero. Capital brings in ₹50,000; rent costs ₹8,000; drawings take ₹3,000. What is the closing cash balance?
Cash = 50,000 − 8,000 − 3,000 = ₹39,000. Positive cash has a debit balance.
Cash opens at ₹10,000 Dr. Cash sales are ₹5,000 and expenses paid are ₹4,000. What is the closing balance?
Opening cash plus receipts minus payments = 10,000 + 5,000 − 4,000 = ₹11,000 Dr.
A customer's account opens at ₹12,000 Dr. A new credit sale is ₹8,000 and collection is ₹15,000. What is the closing balance?
Receivable = 12,000 + 8,000 − 15,000 = ₹5,000 Dr still due from the customer.
A supplier's account opens at ₹20,000 Cr. New credit purchases are ₹7,000 and payment is ₹10,000. What is the closing balance?
Payable = 20,000 + 7,000 − 10,000 = ₹17,000 Cr still owed to the supplier.
Rent Expense has debit postings of ₹4,000 and ₹6,000 with no credits. What is its balance?
Add the debit expense postings: 4,000 + 6,000 = ₹10,000 Dr before closing entries.
Sales Revenue has credits of ₹12,000 and ₹8,000 with no debits. What is its balance?
Total sales credits are ₹20,000, giving a credit balance before closing entries.
A bank ledger has ₹60,000 total debits and ₹45,000 total credits, including all postings. What is the balance?
Debit totals exceed credit totals by ₹15,000, so the balance is debit.
A bank ledger has ₹40,000 total debits and ₹55,000 total credits, including all postings. What does it show?
Credits exceed debits by ₹15,000. A bank credit balance generally indicates an overdraft liability.
In a traditional cash ledger, a receipt from the owner is shown on which side?
Cash is debited when received. The debit-side particular names the corresponding account, Capital.
In a traditional cash ledger, a rent payment is shown on which side?
Cash is credited when paid out. The corresponding rent account appears on the credit side.
What does a debit balance in a customer's receivable ledger normally mean?
The customer has paid more than owed
A debit receivable balance is an asset: money recoverable from the customer.
What does a credit balance in a supplier's payable ledger normally mean?
The supplier owes the business cash
A supplier's credit balance is a liability showing the amount payable.
An ordinary Cash A/c shows a negative balance. What should you do first?
Check for missing receipts or incorrect postings
Accept it as a normal cash overdraft
Physical cash cannot normally be overdrawn. A negative cash balance suggests missing, misdated, or incorrect entries.
Loan Payable opens at ₹1,00,000 Cr. Principal repayments total ₹25,000. What is its closing balance?
Principal repayments debit and reduce the liability: 1,00,000 − 25,000 = ₹75,000 Cr.
Prepaid Insurance opens at ₹12,000 Dr. ₹3,000 of coverage is consumed. What is its remaining asset balance?
Consumption credits the prepaid asset. The remaining future benefit is 12,000 − 3,000 = ₹9,000 Dr.
Salary Payable opens at ₹8,000 Cr. ₹5,000 is paid and ₹2,000 more salary is accrued. What is the closing balance?
A customer owes ₹10,000. Goods worth ₹2,000 are returned and ₹6,000 cash is collected. What remains receivable?
Both returns and collection reduce receivables: 10,000 − 2,000 − 6,000 = ₹2,000 Dr.
A supplier is owed ₹15,000. Goods worth ₹3,000 are returned and ₹10,000 is paid. What remains payable?
Returns and payment debit the payable: 15,000 − 3,000 − 10,000 = ₹2,000 Cr.
An account has total debits of ₹25,000 and total credits of ₹18,000. What is its balance?
The excess debit amount is 25,000 − 18,000 = ₹7,000 Dr.
An account has total credits of ₹30,000 and total debits of ₹12,000. What is its balance?
The excess credit amount is 30,000 − 12,000 = ₹18,000 Cr.
How does ₹5,000 paid to a supplier appear in the supplier's ledger?
As a debit reducing the payable
As a credit increasing the payable
Debit the supplier's account when the business settles an existing payable.
How does ₹4,000 received from a customer appear in the customer's ledger?
As a credit reducing the receivable
As a debit increasing the receivable
As a new sales credit automatically
Credit the customer's account when collecting an existing receivable.
A ₹10,000 credit sale is posted to which two ledgers in a simple example?
A credit sale creates a customer receivable and sales income. Cash is not affected at the time of sale.
Can one ledger contain both debit and credit postings?
Yes; transactions can affect the account in either direction
No; each ledger uses only one side
An account records both increases and decreases as appropriate. Its final balance is the net difference.
Unearned Revenue opens at ₹9,000 Cr. ₹4,000 is earned and a new advance of ₹3,000 is received. What is the closing balance?
Accumulated Depreciation opens at ₹20,000 Cr and this year's depreciation adds ₹5,000. What is the closing balance?
Accumulated depreciation increases with a credit. Its closing contra-asset balance is ₹25,000 Cr.
Which standard Tally Prime voucher records a cash payment of current office rent?
Use Payment for money paid out. Debit Rent Expense and credit Cash.
Which standard Tally Prime voucher records collection against an existing customer invoice?
A Receipt voucher records collection of money. Debit Cash or Bank and credit the customer.
Which standard voucher records depositing business cash into the business bank?
Contra records transfers between cash and bank accounts within the business.
Which standard voucher records a withdrawal from the business bank for office cash?
The transfer is Bank to Cash within the business, so use Contra.
Which standard voucher records goods sold for cash?
Receipt instead of recording the sale
Record the sale in a Sales voucher, even for cash sales. Receipt is used for collecting an existing receivable.
Which standard voucher records goods bought on credit from a supplier?
A Purchase voucher records the supplier's purchase invoice. Later settlement is a Payment voucher.
Which standard voucher is commonly used for a non-cash depreciation adjustment?
Depreciation is an adjustment without a cash movement. A Journal voucher records the expense and asset adjustment.
In standard voucher-entry shortcuts, F4 selects which voucher?
F4 is the standard shortcut for Contra in voucher entry.
In standard voucher-entry shortcuts, F5 selects which voucher?
F5 selects Payment, used for cash or bank payments.
In standard voucher-entry shortcuts, F6 selects which voucher?
F6 selects Receipt, used for cash or bank receipts.
In standard voucher-entry shortcuts, F7 selects which voucher?
F7 selects Journal for general and adjustment entries.
In standard voucher-entry shortcuts, F8 selects which voucher?
F8 selects Sales for sales transactions.
In standard voucher-entry shortcuts, F9 selects which voucher?
F9 selects Purchase for purchase transactions.
A regular customer ledger is usually created under which Tally group?
Customers owing money are grouped under Sundry Debtors, which falls under Current Assets.
A regular supplier ledger is usually created under which Tally group?
Supplier payables are usually grouped under Sundry Creditors, which falls under Current Liabilities.
An ordinary positive-balance bank ledger is normally created under which group?
Use Bank Accounts for an ordinary business bank account. Bank overdraft accounts have a separate appropriate group.
An office-rent expense ledger is normally created under which group?
General office rent is normally an indirect expense. Factory or production-related rent may require different classification.
A machinery asset ledger is normally created under which group?
Machinery used in the business is a fixed asset rather than trading inventory.
An owner's capital ledger is normally created under which group?
Capital contributed by the owner belongs under Capital Account, not sales income.
A sales-of-goods ledger is normally created under which group?
Sales of trading goods are grouped under Sales Accounts.
A purchases-of-trading-goods ledger is normally created under which group?
Trading purchases normally use Purchase Accounts. Assets purchased for business use belong to asset groups.
Which voucher is commonly used to record a customer's sales return?
Debit Note for a purchase return
A sales return normally reduces what the customer owes and is recorded using a Credit Note.
Which voucher is commonly used to record a purchase return to a supplier?
Credit Note for a sales return
A purchase return normally reduces the supplier payable and is recorded using a Debit Note.
Which voucher is appropriate when a supplier's already-recorded invoice is paid by bank?
Use Payment to settle the payable. Recording another Purchase would duplicate the invoice.
Which voucher is commonly used when the owner introduces cash as capital?
A Receipt voucher can record Cash debit and Capital credit for capital introduced in cash.
Which voucher normally records office salaries paid by bank?
Salary payment sends money out for an expense, so use Payment rather than Contra.
Which report shows transactions of one selected account?
A Ledger report groups the postings for a selected account and shows its balance.
Which report is used to inspect vouchers recorded across a selected period?
Day Book lists recorded vouchers for the chosen period and helps inspect individual transactions.
What should be checked before saving a simple double-entry voucher?
Correct ledgers, date, amounts, and equal debit/credit totals
Only the ledger's spelling, ignoring amounts
Balancing is necessary, but the ledgers, transaction date, and amounts must also reflect what actually happened.
Does choosing a Tally ledger group change the fundamental debit/credit rule for the transaction?
No; the transaction and account nature still determine the entry
Yes; every grouped account is credited
Yes; every grouped account is debited
No debit or credit is needed in Tally
Groups control classification and reporting. Correct double-entry logic still applies to each voucher.
What is the basic accounting equation?
Business assets are financed by obligations to outsiders and the owner's equity.
Assets are ₹1,50,000 and liabilities are ₹60,000. What is equity?
Equity is ₹80,000 and liabilities are ₹20,000. What are assets?
Assets are ₹1,20,000 and equity is ₹70,000. What are liabilities?
What must hold for every correctly recorded double-entry transaction?
Double-entry bookkeeping records equal total debit and credit effects for each transaction.
Can one transaction affect more than two accounts?
Yes, if total debits still equal total credits
No, exactly two accounts are always required
Only if cash is not used
Compound entries can include several debit and credit accounts while keeping totals equal.
Which statement about a balanced trial balance is correct?
It does not prove that every transaction is correct
It proves every invoice was recorded
It proves the business earned a profit
Omissions, wrong-account postings, and equal debit/credit mistakes can leave the trial balance balanced.
An entire purchase invoice is omitted from both debit and credit postings. What can happen to the trial balance?
It must differ by twice the invoice
A complete omission removes equal debits and credits, so agreement alone will not detect it.
What does the business-entity concept require?
Treat the business separately from the owner's personal affairs
Treat all personal expenses as business costs
The business has separate books. Owner investments and personal withdrawals are recorded as capital and drawings.
Under accrual accounting, revenue is generally recognised when what happens?
The year-end bank balance is printed
Revenue is recognised when earned under the applicable recognition requirements, which may be before cash collection.
Under accrual accounting, expenses are generally recognised when what happens?
They are incurred for the period
Only when the owner approves a withdrawal
Expenses are recognised when incurred or consumed, even if payment occurs later.
Is a bank loan received normally business revenue?
Yes; all cash receipts are revenue
Yes; only the principal is revenue
No; it creates an expense immediately
Loan proceeds increase cash or bank and create an obligation to repay. They are not earned income.
Are personal drawings normally a business expense?
No; they increase liabilities to customers
Drawings are distributions to the owner and reduce capital rather than business profit through an expense.
A liability is an obligation to pay or provide value. Supplier payables meet that definition.
A receivable is a resource recoverable from a customer and is an asset.
Buying office equipment for cash immediately changes which equation components?
One asset increases and another decreases
Equipment increases and cash decreases. The total asset amount is unchanged at purchase in this simple example.
Taking a bank loan into the business bank account changes which equation components?
Bank funds increase an asset while Loan Payable increases a liability by an equal amount.
The owner introduces additional cash capital. What happens to the accounting equation?
Cash increases assets and the owner's investment increases equity.
Revenue is ₹80,000 and expenses are ₹55,000. What is the profit?
Revenue is ₹40,000 and expenses are ₹48,000. What is the result?
Expenses exceed revenue by ₹8,000, so the business has a loss.
What is the difference between a journal and a ledger?
A journal records events in order; a ledger groups them by account
A journal records only assets; a ledger only liabilities
A journal records only cash; a ledger only credit
They never contain the same transactions
The same double-entry effects are recorded chronologically and then grouped in individual accounts.
Which account is generally temporary and closed at period-end?
Income and expense accounts are temporary. Asset, liability, and equity balances generally carry forward.
Which account is generally permanent and carried forward?
Cash is a balance-sheet asset. Income and expense accounts are closed for the reporting period.
A sale for which payment is due later
A credit sale creates a customer receivable while recognising sales income.
A purchase for which the supplier is paid later
A credit purchase creates a payable to the supplier.
A trade discount reduces an invoice price before recording. How is the purchase usually recorded in a simple example?
At gross value with automatic income for the buyer
Only when the goods are sold
A trade discount is normally reflected in the net transaction price rather than recorded as a separate settlement-discount ledger.
What is the purpose of a journal narration?
To replace the debit and credit amounts
To determine the bank balance automatically
To act as the only source document
A narration explains what was recorded and supports understanding and review; it does not replace the underlying documents.
When a previously recorded customer invoice is collected, should sales revenue be recorded again?
Yes; every receipt is a new sale
Collection changes the receivable into cash or bank. Recording sales again would double-count revenue.
A refundable security deposit paid to a landlord is normally what?
The business expects to recover the deposit, so it is recorded as an asset rather than consumed rent.
Why can profit differ from the cash balance?
Accruals, credit transactions, asset purchases, and financing affect them differently
Profit is always higher than cash
Profit measures income minus expenses; cash also reflects collections, payments, capital, loans, and asset purchases.
